invariant: Mapping binds governed analytical identity to an exact destination object and field edition.
A manifest identifies parsed resource definitions and dependencies for an exact project edition.
A build receipt distinguishes selected, executed, passed, failed and skipped resources.
A captured change preserves source operation, identity, before/after availability and cursor evidence.
A checkpoint binds operator state and source positions; it does not alone prove external exactly-once effects.
A binding names exact source occurrence, connector/profile and scoped credential reference.
A declaration identifies desired access and configuration, never a credential value or source grant.
The consumer-group owner governs assignment-fenced transport progress, not source capture, operator checkpoints or business effects.
Delivery progress records acknowledged source-to-target work and is distinct from source and broker cursors.
A receipt names input cut, sink effect profile and acknowledged target state; it is not a quality certificate.
A destination receipt records observed API effect outcome without asserting downstream business success.
An insert/update/upsert/delete proposal requires separate purpose and destination authority before execution.
The envelope owner governs provider-neutral event metadata, not payload truth, log position, delivery or business acceptance.
Retention bounds broker replay availability and cannot imply source-system history retention.
A logical graph is provider-neutral and distinct from runner plans and workflow task graphs.
Materialization declares desired target behavior and must be lowered against exact adapter capabilities.
Run evidence supports observed derivation only within explicit facet and collection limits.
Operator state is versioned against operator identity, partitioning and serializer compatibility.
The retained-log owner governs log identity, epoch, partition, position and retained ranges, not source cursors or consumer progress.
A snapshot cut records the source visibility boundary and stitching relation to live changes.
Movement preserves or translates a source fact but cannot issue it.
A source-native cursor is not a broker offset, workflow logical date or destination checkpoint.
Retries create distinct attempts; success does not establish data correctness or idempotent effects.
A transport offset locates broker log progress and is never substituted for a source transaction cursor.
A watermark is a progress assertion with lateness assumptions, not wall-clock time or completeness proof.
A workflow orders tasks and conditions but cannot redefine a task's semantic result.
A run is one workflow-definition edition over a logical interval and trigger, distinct from task attempts.
